title: verify_did_sig: verify Ed25519 DID signature over article
description:
What: Implement verify_did_sig() in crates/reader/src/post/did_verify.rs.

Algorithm:
1. pub fn verify_did_sig(article_bytes: &[u8], header_value: &str) -> Result<bool, DidSigError>
   where header_value is the value of X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig: e.g. 'did:key:z6Mk... <base64url-sig>'
2. Split header_value on the LAST space (to allow spaces in did URLs, though did:key has none).
   If fewer than 2 tokens, return DidSigError::InvalidFormat('expected <did-url> <base64url-sig>'.into())
   Let did_url = first part, sig_b64 = last part
3. Decode sig_b64 using base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(sig_b64).
   On error return DidSigError::InvalidSignatureEncoding(e.to_string())
4. Check decoded sig length == 64. If not, return DidSigError::InvalidSignatureEncoding('expected 64-byte Ed25519 sig'.into())
5. Convert sig to ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&sig_arr) where sig_arr: [u8; 64]
6. Call parse_did_key(did_url) -> verifying_key. Propagate error.
7. Strip X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header line from article_bytes to get unsigned_bytes.
   Use a line-by-line approach: split on \r\n (or \n as fallback), discard lines whose lowercase prefix matches 'x-usenet-ipfs-did-sig:', rejoin with \r\n.
   This mirrors extract_sig_header() in sign.rs.
8. Call verifying_key.verify_strict(&unsigned_bytes, &signature). 
   Ok(()) -> return Ok(true)
   Err(_) -> return Ok(false)  [verification failed is not an error, just false]

Defensive programming:
- Verification failure (wrong sig) is Ok(false), not Err — callers distinguish 'could not verify' from 'verified as invalid'
- Do not log sig bytes or key bytes
- The unsigned_bytes stripping must handle both \r\n and \n line endings
- Use ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey::verify_strict (not verify) to reject weak signatures
